words.enDefinition: feeling ready to fall asleep and needing rest

examples.en: I get so sleepy in my 2 p.m. lecture that I start nodding off.
examples.zh: 下午两点的课让我特别「困」，听着听着就打起了瞌睡。

examples.en: Drink something warm if you feel sleepy while revising tonight.
examples.zh: 今晚复习时要是觉得「困」，就喝点热的提提神。

words.enDefinition: half asleep and slow to react, often after medicine

examples.en: The allergy pills made me so drowsy that I skipped my morning seminar.
examples.zh: 抗过敏药让我「昏昏欲睡」，索性翘了早上的讨论课。

examples.en: I felt drowsy all afternoon after staying up past three.
examples.zh: 熬到凌晨三点之后，我一下午都「昏昏欲睡」。

words.enDefinition: aching and painful when touched or used

examples.en: My legs are really sore after yesterday's gym session with Kai.
examples.zh: 昨天和小凯练完力量，我的腿到现在还是「酸痛」的。

examples.en: I've got a sore throat, so I'm drinking honey lemon water.
examples.zh: 我嗓子「疼」得厉害，只能多喝蜂蜜柠檬水。

words.enDefinition: not able to bend or move easily and comfortably

examples.en: Sitting through three back-to-back lectures left my neck really stiff.
examples.zh: 连着上了三节课，我的脖子都「僵」了。

examples.en: New leather shoes always feel stiff until you break them in.
examples.zh: 新皮鞋一开始都「硬邦邦」的，穿一阵子才会合脚。

words.enDefinition: making you want to scratch the skin

examples.en: This wool sweater is so itchy that I took it off halfway through class.
examples.zh: 这件羊毛衫「扎得发痒」，我上到一半就脱了。

examples.en: The mosquito bites on my ankle are itchy and driving me crazy.
examples.zh: 脚踝上的蚊子包「痒」得我受不了。

words.enDefinition: feeling that everything is spinning and you might fall

examples.en: I stood up too fast in the library and felt dizzy for a second.
examples.zh: 在图书馆起身起太快，我「晕」了一下。

examples.en: She skipped breakfast and felt dizzy during her morning lab.
examples.zh: 她没吃早饭，早上做实验时觉得「头晕」。

words.enDefinition: feeling slightly sick in the stomach

examples.en: The long bus ride on mountain roads left me feeling queasy.
examples.zh: 山路大巴坐下来，我有点「恶心想吐」。

examples.en: I felt queasy after eating that leftover sushi from last night.
examples.zh: 吃了昨晚剩的寿司之后，我一直觉得「恶心」。

words.enDefinition: covered in sweat or making you sweat

examples.en: Biking across campus to my seminar left me completely sweaty.
examples.zh: 骑车横穿校园去上讨论课，到教室时我已「满身是汗」。

examples.en: Ten minutes on the treadmill leaves me sweaty because the gym AC is weak.
examples.zh: 这家健身房空调太弱，跑步机上十分钟我就「汗流浃背」。

words.enDefinition: feeling uncomfortably full from eating too much

examples.en: I'm so stuffed from the all-you-can-eat hotpot that I can barely walk.
examples.zh: 自助火锅吃得太狠，我「撑」得快走不动了。

examples.en: Don't order more noodles; I'm already stuffed after that huge lunch.
examples.zh: 别再加面了，午餐那顿我已经吃得很「撑」。

words.enDefinition: moving awkwardly and often dropping or breaking things

examples.en: I'm so clumsy that I knocked my roommate's mug off the desk twice this week.
examples.zh: 我实在太「笨手笨脚」了，这周两次把室友的杯子碰下桌。

examples.en: Clumsy people like me should never carry four plates at once.
examples.zh: 像我这么「笨手笨脚」的人，一次绝不该端四个盘子。

words.enDefinition: having plenty of energy for activity

examples.en: Morning runs leave me feeling energetic instead of groggy in class.
examples.zh: 晨跑让我上课时「精力充沛」，不再昏昏沉沉。

examples.en: My roommate is unbelievably energetic; she hits the gym before her 8 a.m. class.
examples.zh: 我室友「精力充沛」得惊人，八点的课前还先去了趟健身房。

words.enDefinition: often canceling plans or forgetting promises

examples.en: Don't count on Mia to drive us; she's been really flaky lately.
examples.zh: 别指望米娅开车捎我们了，她最近特别「不靠谱」。

examples.en: He's a nice guy but so flaky that he bailed on movie night twice.
examples.zh: 他人不错，就是爱「放鸽子」，电影之夜爽约了两次。

words.enDefinition: relaxed and not easily annoyed or worried

examples.en: My host family is super easygoing, so the house rules are pretty relaxed.
examples.zh: 我的寄宿家庭非常「随和」，家规都很宽松。

examples.en: An easygoing roommate matters more than one who shares your major.
examples.zh: 室友「好相处」比和你专业相同更重要。

words.enDefinition: refusing to change your mind even when wrong

examples.en: My dad is too stubborn to ask for directions even with GPS on.
examples.zh: 我爸「固执」得很，开着导航也不肯问路。

examples.en: She's stubborn about her thesis topic, even after the advisor objected.
examples.zh: 导师提出异议后，她对论文选题依然很「固执」。

words.enDefinition: trying too hard to make people do what you want

examples.en: The salesman got pushy when I said I was just looking around.
examples.zh: 我说只是随便看看，销售就开始「强人所难」。

examples.en: Some club recruiters are way too pushy during welcome week.
examples.zh: 迎新周有些社团招新的同学特别「咄咄逼人」，让人反感。

words.enDefinition: honest and direct about what you think

examples.en: My supervisor is straightforward, so I always know where I stand.
examples.zh: 我的导师「直截了当」，所以我清楚自己所处的位置。

examples.en: Just be straightforward and tell your roommate the dishes bother you.
examples.zh: 有话就「直说」，直接告诉室友碗筷的事让你不舒服。

words.enDefinition: careful not to inconvenience or hurt others

examples.en: It was considerate of Dan to text before inviting people over.
examples.zh: 丹请人来家里前先发消息问一声，真是「体贴」。

examples.en: A considerate roommate wears headphones instead of blasting music late at night.
examples.zh: 「体贴」的室友会戴耳机，而不是深夜外放音乐。

words.enDefinition: unwilling to spend or share money

examples.en: My landlord is so stingy that he refuses to fix the heating properly.
examples.zh: 我房东「小气」得很，都不肯好好修暖气。

examples.en: Don't be stingy with the cheese; we already bought a whole bag.
examples.zh: 芝士别放得那么「抠」，我们可是买了一整袋。

words.enDefinition: too interested in other people's private business

examples.en: My neighbor is nice but nosy; she always asks who was visiting me.
examples.zh: 邻居人不错就是「爱打听」，总问谁来找我。

examples.en: Quit being nosy about my grades; that's between me and my advisor.
examples.zh: 别对我的成绩「打破砂锅问到底」，那是我和导师之间的事。

words.enDefinition: doubting that something is true or useful

examples.en: I was skeptical about the tutoring service until my grades improved.
examples.zh: 一开始我对那家辅导机构是「怀疑」的，直到成绩真的提高。

examples.en: Professors stay skeptical of sources that have no author listed.
examples.zh: 教授们对没有署名的资料来源持「怀疑」态度。

words.enDefinition: keeping plans, files, and time neatly arranged

examples.en: Nina is so organized that she color-codes every deadline in her planner.
examples.zh: 妮娜做事特别「有条理」，每个截止日期都用颜色标进计划本。

examples.en: Staying organized during finals week saves you a lot of panic.
examples.zh: 期末周保持「有条理」，能省去很多手忙脚乱。

words.enDefinition: doing dangerous things without thinking about the results

examples.en: Cycling down that hill with no brakes was honestly pretty reckless.
examples.zh: 骑没闸的自行车冲下那个坡，说实话挺「鲁莽」的。

examples.en: He was reckless with his credit card during orientation week.
examples.zh: 迎新周那会儿他刷信用卡毫无节制，太「鲁莽」了。

words.enDefinition: large inside, with plenty of room to move

examples.en: The shared kitchen is surprisingly spacious, so four of us cook together.
examples.zh: 公共厨房意外地「宽敞」，我们四个人能一起做饭。

examples.en: This studio looks spacious because the bed folds into the wall.
examples.zh: 这间开间看着「宽敞」，因为床可以折进墙里。

words.enDefinition: too small and tight to move around comfortably

examples.en: Four people in one dorm room gets cramped really fast.
examples.zh: 一间宿舍住四个人很快就显得「拥挤」。

examples.en: My desk is so cramped that the lamp and laptop barely fit.
examples.zh: 我的书桌「逼仄」得很，台灯和电脑都差点放不下。

words.enDefinition: small, warm, and comfortable in a pleasant way

examples.en: With fairy lights and a hot water bottle, my room feels really cozy.
examples.zh: 装上串灯、抱着暖水袋，我的房间「温馨」极了。

examples.en: This cafe is cozy on rainy afternoons, so I always study here.
examples.zh: 雨天下午这家咖啡馆「温馨」又舒服，我总来这里学习。

words.enDefinition: warm and close, with no fresh air moving

examples.en: Open a window; the study room gets stuffy by mid-afternoon.
examples.zh: 开扇窗吧，自习室一到下午就「闷」了。

examples.en: I almost fell asleep because the lecture hall was so stuffy.
examples.zh: 阶梯教室「闷」得我差点睡着。

words.enDefinition: letting cold outside air in through gaps

examples.en: This old building is so drafty that we tape towels over the window frames.
examples.zh: 这栋老楼「漏风」厉害，我们只能用毛巾塞住窗缝。

examples.en: My bed sits under a drafty window, so I sleep in a hoodie.
examples.zh: 床正对一扇「透风」的窗，我只能穿着连帽衫睡。

words.enDefinition: slightly wet in an unpleasant, clammy way

examples.en: The basement bedroom feels damp even after we run the dehumidifier.
examples.zh: 即使开了除湿机，地下室卧室还是「潮」的。

examples.en: Hang your towel outside; it went damp in the closet again.
examples.zh: 毛巾晾出去吧，在柜子里又「受潮」了。

words.enDefinition: covered with mold from staying too wet

examples.en: I found a moldy sandwich behind the mini fridge during deep cleaning.
examples.zh: 大扫除时我在小冰箱后面发现一个「发霉」的三明治。

examples.en: The shower curtain went moldy, so we bought a new one.
examples.zh: 浴帘「发霉」了，我们买了条新的。

words.enDefinition: covered with a layer of fine dry dirt

examples.en: The top shelf is so dusty that I sneeze every time I clean it.
examples.zh: 顶层架子「积灰」严重，每次清理都打喷嚏。

examples.en: My laptop fan got dusty, so the whole thing runs loud now.
examples.zh: 笔记本风扇「积」了不少灰，现在一开机就嗡嗡响。

words.enDefinition: full of too many things spread around untidily

examples.en: My desk gets cluttered with receipts, cables, and half-finished coffee.
examples.zh: 我桌上「堆满」小票、数据线和喝了一半的咖啡。

examples.en: The shared fridge is cluttered, so nothing ever fits inside.
examples.zh: 公共冰箱塞得「乱七八糟」，什么都放不进去。

words.enDefinition: arranged neatly, with everything in its place

examples.en: Keep the common room tidy, or the RA will send a reminder email.
examples.zh: 公共活动室要保持「整洁」，不然宿管会发提醒邮件。

examples.en: Her kitchen stays tidy even while she cooks for ten people.
examples.zh: 就算同时给十个人做饭，她的厨房也一直「整整齐齐」。

words.enDefinition: not neat, with things left everywhere

examples.en: Sorry the floor is messy; I pulled out all my winter clothes.
examples.zh: 抱歉地上「乱糟糟」的，我把冬装全翻出来了。

examples.en: He's a lovely roommate, just a bit messy about the dishes.
examples.zh: 他人挺好，就是在碗筷上有点「邋遢」。

words.enDefinition: extremely dirty and unpleasant to look at

examples.en: The shared microwave was filthy, so we put up a cleaning schedule.
examples.zh: 公共微波炉「脏」得不行，我们贴了张清洁轮值表。

examples.en: After moving that old sofa, my hands and sleeves were absolutely filthy.
examples.zh: 挪完那个旧沙发，我的手和袖子「脏」得不像话。

words.enDefinition: perfectly clean, with no dirt at all

examples.en: My roommate scrubbed the kitchen until it was completely spotless.
examples.zh: 室友把厨房擦得「一尘不染」。

examples.en: Landlords expect the flat spotless when you hand back the keys.
examples.zh: 退房交钥匙时，房东要求屋子「一尘不染」。

words.enDefinition: not bright, so it is hard to see clearly

examples.en: The stairwell light is so dim that I tripped on my backpack twice.
examples.zh: 楼道灯太「昏暗」，我两次被自己的背包绊到。

examples.en: This dim corner of the library is great for napping, not for reading.
examples.zh: 图书馆这个「昏暗」角落适合打盹，不适合看书。

words.enDefinition: having enough light to see and work comfortably

examples.en: Choose a well-lit bus stop at night so drivers can see you.
examples.zh: 晚上等车要选「光线好」的站台，司机才看得见你。

examples.en: I study in the well-lit reading room because my eyes get tired downstairs.
examples.zh: 我在「光线明亮」的阅览室学习，在楼下待久了眼睛累。

words.enDefinition: cooled and kept fresh by air conditioning

examples.en: The library is air-conditioned, so everyone camps there during heat waves.
examples.zh: 图书馆「有空调」，热浪一来大家都去那儿待着。

examples.en: Only the computer labs are air-conditioned; our dorm room just has a fan.
examples.zh: 只有机房「有空调」，我们宿舍只有一台风扇。

words.enDefinition: built so that sound cannot pass through

examples.en: The music rooms are soundproof, so band practice runs until midnight.
examples.zh: 琴房「隔音」很好，乐队排练能到半夜。

examples.en: I wish our dorm walls were soundproof; I hear every karaoke night.
examples.zh: 真希望宿舍墙能「隔音」，隔壁的 K 歌之夜我全听见了。

words.enDefinition: allowing tenants or guests to keep animals

examples.en: Most student housing isn't pet-friendly, so my cat lives with my aunt.
examples.zh: 多数学生公寓「不允许养宠物」，我的猫只好寄养在姑姑家。

examples.en: We found a pet-friendly cafe where dogs get free biscuits.
examples.zh: 我们找到一家「宠物友好」咖啡馆，狗狗还能领免费饼干。

words.enDefinition: close enough that you can reach places on foot

examples.en: I picked this flat because campus and two supermarkets are walkable.
examples.zh: 选这套房子，就是看中去校园和两家超市都能「步行到达」。

examples.en: The riverside area is walkable, unlike the dorms up on the hill.
examples.zh: 河边的街区适合「步行」，山腰的宿舍区就差远了。

words.enDefinition: full of tourists and shops aimed at them

examples.en: The old harbor is pretty touristy, so prices double near the water.
examples.zh: 老码头一带「游客扎堆」，海边的价格翻倍。

examples.en: Skip the touristy streets; the food two blocks inland is better.
examples.zh: 别去「游客扎堆」的那几条街，往里走两个街区的吃的更好。

words.enDefinition: completely full of people with no space left

examples.en: The gym gets packed right after five, so I go before my first class.
examples.zh: 健身房五点后「人满为患」，所以我第一节课前先去。

examples.en: The dining hall was so packed that we ate standing by the window.
examples.zh: 食堂「挤」得水泄不通，我们只能靠窗站着吃。

words.enDefinition: old and in poor condition from neglect

examples.en: The building looks rundown outside, but the flat inside is actually fine.
examples.zh: 楼从外面看挺「破旧」，里面的公寓倒还行。

examples.en: They raised the rent on a rundown place with the same broken elevator.
examples.zh: 电梯坏着不修，这么「破」的房子居然还涨租。

words.enDefinition: useful and easy to use or reach

examples.en: This little key light is handy when I cycle home after sunset.
examples.zh: 日落后骑车回家，这盏小钥匙灯特别「好用」。

examples.en: Keep a power strip handy; dorm outlets are never where you need them.
examples.zh: 插线板要放在「随手能拿到」的地方，宿舍插座总不在你需要的位置。

words.enDefinition: strong and well made, not easily broken

examples.en: Buy a sturdy umbrella here; the cheap ones die in one storm.
examples.zh: 在这儿买把「结实」的伞，便宜的撑不过一场暴雨。

examples.en: You'll need sturdy shelves to hold all these engineering textbooks.
examples.zh: 这些工科教材很沉，得用「结实」的书架才放得住。

words.enDefinition: thin and light, likely to break easily

examples.en: The flimsy plastic hangers snap the moment you hang a wet coat.
examples.zh: 这种「不结实」的塑料衣架，挂件湿外套就断。

examples.en: That flimsy folding chair scared me every time I sat on it.
examples.zh: 那把「不结实」的折叠椅，每次坐上去我都心惊胆战。

words.enDefinition: big and heavy, hard to carry or store

examples.en: Winter coats are bulky, so we vacuum-seal them under the bed each spring.
examples.zh: 冬衣「笨重」，每年开春我们都抽真空压到床底。

examples.en: Shipping a bulky desk across the city costs more than a new one.
examples.zh: 把「笨重」的书桌横穿城市运一趟，比买张新的还贵。

words.enDefinition: small and neatly arranged to save space

examples.en: This compact rice cooker fits on the tiniest dorm shelf.
examples.zh: 这款「小巧」的电饭煲连宿舍最小的架子都放得下。

examples.en: I keep a compact umbrella in my bag because weather here flips fast.
examples.zh: 我包里常备一把「小巧」的伞，这儿天气说变就变。

words.enDefinition: easy to carry or move from place to place

examples.en: A portable monitor makes group work on the quad actually possible.
examples.zh: 有了「便携」显示器，在草坪上搞小组作业才真正可行。

examples.en: She brought a portable fan to the packed lecture hall.
examples.zh: 她带了台「便携」小风扇去挤满人的阶梯教室。

words.enDefinition: able to be changed to fit different needs

examples.en: Get an adjustable desk lamp so late readings don't wake your roommate.
examples.zh: 买盏「可调节」的台灯，夜里赶阅读就不吵到室友。

examples.en: The chair's adjustable arms saved my shoulders during thesis season.
examples.zh: 写论文那阵子，椅子「可调」的扶手救了我的肩膀。

words.enDefinition: not straight or level, bent to one side

examples.en: The picture frames in our hallway hang crooked because the walls tilt.
examples.zh: 走廊里的相框都挂「歪」了，因为墙本身是斜的。

examples.en: He grinned with one crooked tooth showing, right before his presentation.
examples.zh: 展示前一刻，他咧嘴一笑，露出一颗「歪」牙。

words.enDefinition: not firmly fixed or attached in place

examples.en: One loose screw makes the whole chair wobble during exam week.
examples.zh: 一颗「松动」的螺丝，让整把椅子在考试周晃个不停。

examples.en: My charger cable is loose, so it only charges at one angle.
examples.zh: 充电线的接口「松」了，只有摆一个角度才能充上电。

words.enDefinition: moving or feeling unsteady from side to side

examples.en: The table in the back corner is shaky, so our coffee keeps spilling.
examples.zh: 后面角落那张桌子「晃」，咖啡一直往外洒。

examples.en: My voice felt shaky during the first minute of the presentation.
examples.zh: 课堂展示的第一分钟，我的声音都在「发颤」。

words.enDefinition: having thin damage lines but not fully broken

examples.en: My cracked phone screen finally gave out during exam week.
examples.zh: 考试周里，我这台「裂了屏」的手机终于罢工了。

examples.en: We tossed the cracked mug rather than risk hot tea leaking everywhere.
examples.zh: 我们把「有裂纹」的马克杯扔了，免得热茶漏得到处都是。

words.enDefinition: with a small piece broken off the edge

examples.en: I still use that chipped blue bowl from the free table outside.
examples.zh: 门口免费桌上那只「掉了瓷」的蓝碗我还在用。

examples.en: Be careful with the chipped edge on that glass; it cuts fingers easily.
examples.zh: 小心那个玻璃杯的「缺口」，很容易划到手。

words.enDefinition: marked with thin surface lines or scrapes

examples.en: The secondhand laptop was cheap because the lid is badly scratched.
examples.zh: 这台二手笔记本便宜，就因为顶盖「划痕」很重。

examples.en: Our landlord charged us for a scratched door that was already like that.
examples.zh: 那扇门本来就是「花」的，房东还照样收我们钱。

words.enDefinition: ripped, with a hole or split in it

examples.en: My backpack strap is torn, so the library books hang at an angle.
examples.zh: 书包带「磨破」了，图书馆借的书都斜挂着。

examples.en: He showed up to the interview with a torn jacket and still got the job.
examples.zh: 他穿着「破」了的夹克去面试，居然还是拿到了那份工作。

words.enDefinition: marked by spots that are hard to wash out

examples.en: The white shirt came back from the wash still stained with coffee.
examples.zh: 白衬衫洗完回来还是「沾着」咖啡渍。

examples.en: We lost part of the deposit over a stained mattress.
examples.zh: 床垫「有污渍」，押金被扣了一部分。

words.enDefinition: having lost color through washing or sunlight

examples.en: My favorite hoodie is so faded that the logo is barely visible.
examples.zh: 我最爱的连帽衫「褪色」严重，logo 都快看不见了。

examples.en: The faded curtains make the whole room look older than it is.
examples.zh: 窗帘「褪」了色，整个房间显得比实际更旧。

words.enDefinition: damaged or thin from being used a long time

examples.en: These running shoes are so worn out that my knees started hurting.
examples.zh: 这双跑鞋「磨」得太旧，我的膝盖都开始疼了。

examples.en: The couch came with the flat and is completely worn out.
examples.zh: 沙发是房东留下的，已经「旧」得不成样子。

words.enDefinition: completely new and never used by anyone

examples.en: I saved two months of tutoring pay for this brand new laptop.
examples.zh: 这台「崭新」的笔记本，我攒了两个月家教工资。

examples.en: Someone left a brand new rice cooker in the free pile outside.
examples.zh: 门口免费堆里有人放了一口「全新」的电饭煲。

words.enDefinition: previously owned or used by someone else

examples.en: Almost all my kitchen stuff is secondhand from graduating seniors.
examples.zh: 我的厨房用品几乎都是毕业生甩卖的「二手货」。

examples.en: Buying secondhand textbooks saved me around three hundred this term.
examples.zh: 这学期买「二手」教材省了差不多三百块。

words.enDefinition: in perfect condition with no damage at all

examples.en: The listing promised pristine condition, and the bike really looks it.
examples.zh: 广告说车况「完好如新」，这辆自行车确实如此。

examples.en: Her resale phone was pristine, without a single scratch on the screen.
examples.zh: 她转卖的手机「九九新」，屏幕上一道划痕都没有。

words.enDefinition: easily broken or damaged if dropped or knocked

examples.en: Mark the box fragile or the movers will stack textbooks on it.
examples.zh: 箱子上要标「易碎」，不然搬家工人会把教材摞在上面。

examples.en: That teacup from my grandma is far too fragile for the dishwasher.
examples.zh: 外婆给的茶杯太「易碎」，不能放进洗碗机。

words.enDefinition: covered or cooked with too much oil

examples.en: The late-night fried chicken is delicious but so greasy that I regret it by midnight.
examples.zh: 深夜炸鸡是真香，但「油」得我到半夜就开始后悔。

examples.en: My hands got greasy fixing the bike chain, and soap barely helped.
examples.zh: 修自行车链条弄得满手「油」，肥皂都几乎洗不掉。

words.enDefinition: having a fine edge that cuts easily

examples.en: Bring a sharp knife to cooking club; dull ones slip and cause cuts.
examples.zh: 烹饪社要带「锋利」的刀，钝刀反而容易打滑伤手。

examples.en: There's a sharp edge on the broken shelf, so tape it over.
examples.zh: 坏掉的架子边缘很「利」，先用胶带缠一下。

words.enDefinition: made so that water cannot get through it

examples.en: Get a waterproof phone pouch for the kayak trip next weekend.
examples.zh: 下周末去划皮划艇，买个「防水」手机袋。

examples.en: These boots claim to be waterproof, yet my socks got soaked anyway.
examples.zh: 这靴子号称「防水」，结果袜子照样湿透。

words.enDefinition: connecting or working without any wires or cables

examples.en: A wireless keyboard frees up half of my tiny dorm desk.
examples.zh: 「无线」键盘能省出我那张小书桌的一半地方。

examples.en: Our wireless earbuds keep disconnecting on the bus route home.
examples.zh: 回家那路公交上，我们的「无线」耳机老是断连。

words.enDefinition: able to be refilled with power and reused

examples.en: I switched to rechargeable batteries for my mouse and keyboard.
examples.zh: 鼠标键盘的电池，我换成了「可充电」的。

examples.en: Pack rechargeable batteries for the trip; the campsite shop charges a fortune.
examples.zh: 出行带上「充电电池」，营地商店的价钱贵得离谱。

words.enDefinition: often stopping working or behaving strangely

examples.en: The quiz platform gets glitchy when two hundred students log in at once.
examples.zh: 两百人同时登录时，测验平台就「频出故障」。

examples.en: My laptop has been glitchy since the update, freezing every few minutes.
examples.zh: 更新之后我的笔记本就「毛病不断」，几分钟卡一次。

words.enDefinition: slow to respond, with noticeable delays between actions

examples.en: The dorm Wi-Fi gets laggy every evening when everyone streams at once.
examples.zh: 每晚大家同时刷视频，宿舍 Wi-Fi 就「卡」得不行。

examples.en: My old phone is so laggy that group video calls are impossible.
examples.zh: 我的旧手机「卡」得厉害，开小组视频通话纯属受罪。

words.enDefinition: able to work together with another device or system

examples.en: Check that the adapter is compatible with your laptop before checkout.
examples.zh: 结账前先确认转接头和你的笔记本「兼容」。

examples.en: The free editing software isn't compatible with my Chromebook, unfortunately.
examples.zh: 可惜这款免费剪辑软件跟我的 Chromebook「不兼容」。

words.enDefinition: happening or available immediately, without any delay

examples.en: Campus chat groups give instant answers about which bus to catch.
examples.zh: 坐哪路车的问题，校园群里都能得到「即时」回复。

examples.en: Instant noodles are my backup plan whenever the dining hall closes early.
examples.zh: 食堂早关门时，我的备用方案就是「泡面」。

words.enDefinition: no longer modern or useful because things have moved on

examples.en: The department's style guide is outdated; it still wants 2005-era footnotes.
examples.zh: 系里的写作规范「过时」了，还要求 2005 年那套脚注格式。

examples.en: My outdated phone can't run the app our seminar requires.
examples.zh: 我的手机太「旧」，跑不动讨论课要求的那个应用。

words.enDefinition: old or old-fashioned in an attractive way

examples.en: I found a vintage denim jacket at the flea market for eight dollars.
examples.zh: 我在跳蚤市场花八块钱淘到一件「复古」牛仔外套。

examples.en: Her vintage film camera is older than both of us combined.
examples.zh: 她那台「老式」胶片相机比我们俩岁数加起来还大。

words.enDefinition: attractive in a way that shows good modern taste

examples.en: A thrifted blazer looks surprisingly stylish with plain jeans and sneakers.
examples.zh: 二手西装外套配素色牛仔裤和小白鞋，会意外地「时髦」。

examples.en: Our TA manages to stay stylish even in a baggy lab coat.
examples.zh: 助教哪怕套着宽松的实验服也照样「有型」。

words.enDefinition: looking cheap and showing poor taste

examples.en: The club's neon banner is a bit tacky, but it photographs well.
examples.zh: 社团那条霓虹横幅有点「俗」，但拍照效果不错。

examples.en: Glitter phone cases felt tacky in high school, yet here I am.
examples.zh: 亮片手机壳高中时我觉得挺「土」，结果现在真香。

words.enDefinition: with a lot of wind blowing outside

examples.en: It's too windy for the rooftop picnic; everything keeps blowing away.
examples.zh: 今天外面「风很大」，天台野餐的东西老被吹跑。

examples.en: Hold your umbrella right; the lakeside path gets really windy at dusk.
examples.zh: 伞要抓稳，傍晚的湖边小路「风」特别大。

words.enDefinition: extremely hot and very uncomfortable to be in

examples.en: The top-floor bedroom is boiling every afternoon until the sun sets.
examples.zh: 顶楼卧室每天下午都「热」到日落才消停。

examples.en: I'm boiling in this sweater; the forecast completely lied to us.
examples.zh: 穿这件毛衣我都「热」冒烟了，天气预报纯属骗人。

words.enDefinition: covered in lines and folds that need ironing

examples.en: My interview shirt came out of the suitcase completely wrinkled.
examples.zh: 面试的衬衫从行李箱里拿出来，已经「皱」得不成样子。

examples.en: She irons everything she owns, so nothing in her closet is wrinkled.
examples.zh: 她的衣服件件都熨，衣柜里找不出一件「起皱」的。

words.enDefinition: making a short high noise when moved or pressed

examples.en: My desk chair is so squeaky that everyone turns around in the library.
examples.zh: 我的椅子「吱嘎」响得厉害，在图书馆里人人都回头。

examples.en: The squeaky door hinge needs a drop of oil before the neighbors complain.
examples.zh: 趁邻居还没投诉，先给「吱嘎」响的合页滴几滴油。

words.enDefinition: letting liquid or air escape through a hole

examples.en: The leaky faucet in our shared kitchen wasted a whole bucket overnight.
examples.zh: 公共厨房那个「漏水」的水龙头，一晚上漏了满满一桶。

examples.en: We reported the leaky ceiling to the landlord twice before it got fixed.
examples.zh: 「漏水」的天花板我们向房东报修了两次才修好。

words.enDefinition: able to be used again instead of thrown away

examples.en: Bring a reusable cup and the campus cafe knocks ten percent off.
examples.zh: 自带「可重复使用」的杯子，校园咖啡馆还打九折。

examples.en: I pack reusable shopping bags so I never buy plastic at the store.
examples.zh: 我总在包里放几个「环保」购物袋，就省得在店里买塑料袋。

words.enDefinition: made to be used once and then thrown away

examples.en: The lab hands out disposable gloves, so nobody shares a dirty pair.
examples.zh: 实验室发「一次性」手套，谁也不用共用脏的那副。

examples.en: We ran out of disposable chopsticks during the club fundraiser lunch.
examples.zh: 社团义卖午餐时，「一次性」筷子都用完了。

words.enDefinition: raining lightly and steadily with fine drops

examples.en: It's drizzly all week, so my canvas shoes never fully dry.
examples.zh: 整周都「下毛毛雨」，帆布鞋就没干透过。

examples.en: A drizzly Sunday is perfect for the library and hot soup.
examples.zh: 「细雨绵绵」的周日正适合泡图书馆、喝热汤。

words.enDefinition: able to stretch and return to its shape

examples.en: These stretchy gym leggings survive every squat without going see-through.
examples.zh: 这条「弹力好」的健身裤深蹲也不会变透。

examples.en: Wear something stretchy for the long flight; jeans get uncomfortable.
examples.zh: 长途飞机穿「有弹性」的裤子吧，牛仔裤坐着难受。

words.enDefinition: covered in wet, soft dirt that sticks to shoes

examples.en: The shortcut across the field turns muddy after every rainstorm.
examples.zh: 每次暴雨过后，穿田的那条近路就「泥泞」不堪。

examples.en: My white sneakers came back muddy from the interdepartmental soccer match.
examples.zh: 踢完院系足球赛，我的小白鞋「糊满」了泥。

words.enDefinition: tasting of almost nothing, without much flavor

examples.en: The cafeteria soup is so bland that everyone adds chili oil.
examples.zh: 食堂的汤「寡淡无味」，人人都要加辣椒油。

examples.en: Bland protein shakes go down easier if you blend in a banana.
examples.zh: 「没味道」的蛋白奶昔里打根香蕉，就好咽多了。

words.enDefinition: no longer fresh, hard or dry as a result

examples.en: The free-box bagels had gone stale, but toasting fixed them.
examples.zh: 免费箱里的贝果已经「不新鲜」了，烤一下还能吃。

examples.en: Stale chips at the bottom of the bag are a student rite of passage.
examples.zh: 吃到最后袋底那些「走了气」的薯片，算是学生的必修课。

words.enDefinition: unpleasantly soft and wet from soaking in liquid

examples.en: Leave your cereal too long and it turns completely soggy.
examples.zh: 麦片泡太久就会「泡」得软塌塌的。

examples.en: The fries arrived soggy because the delivery took forty minutes.
examples.zh: 外卖走了四十分钟，薯条送到时已经「软塌塌」的了。

words.enDefinition: damaged by too much heat, blackened on the outside

examples.en: I burnt the garlic again, so the whole kitchen smells bitter.
examples.zh: 我又把蒜「炒糊」了，整个厨房一股苦味。

examples.en: Slightly burnt toast still counts as breakfast when you're running late.
examples.zh: 赶时间的话，「烤糊」一点的吐司也算早饭。

words.enDefinition: making you feel full for a long time

examples.en: Oatmeal with peanut butter is cheap and really filling before evening labs.
examples.zh: 燕麦加花生酱便宜又「顶饱」，撑到晚上做实验都没问题。

examples.en: The salad bar looks healthy but isn't filling enough after practice.
examples.zh: 沙拉吧看着健康，训练完吃却「不扛饿」。

words.enDefinition: making you feel fresh and less tired

examples.en: An iced americano is so refreshing before a two-hour statistics lecture.
examples.zh: 上两小时的统计课前，一杯冰美式特别「提神」。

examples.en: The lake water was freezing but incredibly refreshing after the run.
examples.zh: 湖水冰凉，跑完步跳进去却「无比清爽」。

words.enDefinition: firm and making a crunch when bitten

examples.en: The fried chicken stays crispy only if you eat it immediately.
examples.zh: 炸鸡只有趁热吃才「酥脆」。

examples.en: Roast the potatoes longer if you want them extra crispy.
examples.zh: 想让土豆「烤」得焦脆，就多烤一会儿。

words.enDefinition: containing plenty of juice or liquid

examples.en: These campus-market peaches are so juicy that I eat them over the sink.
examples.zh: 校集市集的水蜜桃「汁水十足」，我都站在水池边吃。

examples.en: Low heat keeps the braised pork juicy instead of dry and chewy.
examples.zh: 小火慢炖，红烧肉才会「汁多」不柴。

words.enDefinition: made at home rather than bought ready-made

examples.en: My mom mails me homemade chili sauce every single month.
examples.zh: 我妈每个月都给我寄「自制」辣酱。

examples.en: On every cold night, homemade dumplings beat anything the cafeteria sells.
examples.zh: 每个寒冷的夜晚，「家里包」的饺子都完胜食堂。

words.enDefinition: past the printed date for safety or validity

examples.en: Check your passport before booking flights; mine expired last spring.
examples.zh: 订机票前查查护照，我的已经「过期」，去年春天的事。

examples.en: I tossed the expired yogurt rather than risk a rough night.
examples.zh: 那盒「过期」酸奶我还是扔了，免得夜里遭罪。

words.enDefinition: no longer good to eat because it went bad

examples.en: The milk smelled spoiled even though the date said three more days.
examples.zh: 牛奶闻着「变味」了，可保质期明明还剩三天。

examples.en: A spoiled tomato at the bottom of the bag ruined the others.
examples.zh: 袋子底下一个「坏」番茄，把其他的都带坏了。

words.enDefinition: cooked too briefly and still raw inside

examples.en: The chicken was undercooked in the middle, so we sent it back.
examples.zh: 鸡肉中间「没熟」，我们退了这道菜。

examples.en: Undercooked rice gets fixed with ten extra minutes and a splash of water.
examples.zh: 饭「夹生」了就加点水再焖十分钟。

words.enDefinition: costing more than you would like to pay

examples.en: The boba place near campus is pricey, so we go on discount days.
examples.zh: 校门口那家奶茶店「小贵」，所以我们专挑打折日去。

examples.en: Dorm meal plans are pricey compared with cooking with roommates.
examples.zh: 和室友搭伙做饭相比，宿舍的餐饮套餐「偏贵」。

words.enDefinition: priced low enough for you to pay

examples.en: We finally found an affordable flat twenty minutes from campus.
examples.zh: 我们终于找到一套离校园二十分钟、租金「能负担」的房子。

examples.en: Shopping secondhand keeps a professional wardrobe affordable on a student budget.
examples.zh: 买二手衣服，学生预算也「负担」得起职业装。

words.enDefinition: priced too high for what you get

examples.en: That campus bookstore is overpriced; order your books online instead.
examples.zh: 校园书店「定价太高」，教材还是网上下单吧。

examples.en: The coffee is decent but the pastries are honestly overpriced.
examples.zh: 咖啡还行，可那些糕点真是「贵得离谱」。

words.enDefinition: able to be paid back if you cancel

examples.en: Book a refundable train ticket in case the seminar moves.
examples.zh: 讨论课可能改时间，先订「可退」的火车票吧。

examples.en: The deposit is refundable if the walls have no new holes.
examples.zh: 只要墙面没有新钉孔，押金是「可退」的。

words.enDefinition: able to change easily to fit different situations

examples.en: My shift schedule is flexible, so I can swap Fridays with Priya.
examples.zh: 我的班表很「灵活」，周五可以和普丽娅换班。

examples.en: Keep your weekend plans flexible until the group project settles.
examples.zh: 小组作业没定下来之前，周末安排先「灵活」一点。

words.enDefinition: not required; you decide whether to do it

examples.en: The Thursday review session is optional, but it genuinely helps.
examples.zh: 周四的复习课「自愿参加」，不过真的有用。

examples.en: Attendance at the guest lecture is optional and won't affect grades.
examples.zh: 嘉宾讲座「可以自愿」出席，不影响成绩。

words.enDefinition: good enough to justify the cost or effort

examples.en: The 6 a.m. wake-up hurt, but the sunrise hike was worth it.
examples.zh: 早上六点起床确实痛苦，但那次日出徒步「值了」。

examples.en: Rent near campus is high, but being ten minutes from everything is worth it.
examples.zh: 校外房租是贵，但去哪儿都只要十分钟，「值了」。

words.enDefinition: possible to finish or achieve within your ability

examples.en: The reading load looks scary but is doable if you start Friday.
examples.zh: 阅读量看着吓人，周五就开始的话还是「做得完」的。

examples.en: Cycling to both jobs is doable only while the weather holds.
examples.zh: 只有天气好的时候，骑车赶两份工才「行得通」。

words.enDefinition: easy enough to control, handle, or deal with

examples.en: Twelve credits feels manageable now that I dropped the fourth course.
examples.zh: 退掉第四门课后，十二个学分就显得「应付得来」了。

examples.en: Break the essay into steps and the workload stays manageable.
examples.zh: 把论文拆成几步来做，工作量就「在承受范围内」。

words.enDefinition: very busy, with a lot happening fast

examples.en: Move-in weekend was hectic, with elevators packed and boxes everywhere.
examples.zh: 搬入那个周末特别「忙乱」，电梯挤满人，纸箱堆得到处都是。

examples.en: My Thursdays run hectic: lab until four, then work, then seminar reading.
examples.zh: 我的周四「连轴转」：实验到四点，接着上班，还要读研讨课材料。

words.enDefinition: lasting or seeming to last forever without stopping

examples.en: Revision felt endless until we split the past papers across the group.
examples.zh: 刷题一度「没完没了」，后来我们把历年卷分给全组才轻松些。

examples.en: Bus detours turned a short commute into an endless wait.
examples.zh: 公交绕路让短短的通勤变成「没完没了」的等待。

words.enDefinition: having no useful result, purpose, or effect

examples.en: Cramming at 3 a.m. is pointless; sleep helps your memory more.
examples.zh: 凌晨三点临时抱佛脚「没意义」，睡觉对记忆更有用。

examples.en: It feels pointless to format the bibliography twice, so follow the guide first.
examples.zh: 参考文献排两遍太「白费功夫」，先看好规范再动手。

words.enDefinition: taking a lot of time to finish

examples.en: Transcribing the whole interview myself was time-consuming but weirdly calming.
examples.zh: 自己转录访谈很「费时间」，但莫名让人平静。

examples.en: Sunday meal prep saves me from time-consuming cooking every weeknight.
examples.zh: 周日备好菜，省得每个工作日晚上「耗时」做饭。

words.enDefinition: needing a lot of physical effort and energy

examples.en: Nothing strenuous after the flu shot, the nurse said, so I just walked.
examples.zh: 护士说打完流感疫苗别做「剧烈」运动，于是我只散了步。

examples.en: The trail got strenuous halfway up, and we stopped for water.
examples.zh: 爬到半山腰那段特别「费劲」，我们停下来补水。

words.enDefinition: giving something valuable for the effort you put in

examples.en: Volunteering at the writing center is slow going but deeply rewarding.
examples.zh: 在写作中心做志愿进展缓慢，却让我「收获满满」。

examples.en: The research internship was rewarding once I finally understood the data.
examples.zh: 等我终于看懂数据，这段科研实习就「很值」了。

words.enDefinition: making you extremely tired, using up all your energy

examples.en: Orientation week was exhausting; I slept eleven hours on Saturday.
examples.zh: 迎新周「累」得够呛，周六我一觉睡了十一个小时。

examples.en: Carrying boxes up to a fifth-floor walk-up is utterly exhausting.
examples.zh: 把箱子扛上没有电梯的五楼，真是「累」到虚脱。

words.enDefinition: unsafe or probably dishonest; hard to trust

examples.en: That listing with no photos and cheap rent looks totally sketchy.
examples.zh: 那个房源没照片租金还便宜，看着就特别「可疑」。

examples.en: The alley shortcut feels sketchy after dark, so I take the main road.
examples.zh: 天黑后抄小巷让人「心里发毛」，我还是走大路。

words.enDefinition: good enough or acceptable, though not excellent

examples.en: The food truck by the library is decent, especially the falafel wrap.
examples.zh: 图书馆旁那辆餐车味道「还行」，尤其推荐鹰嘴豆丸卷饼。

examples.en: He speaks decent Japanese after one exchange semester in Osaka.
examples.zh: 在大阪交换一学期后，他的日语说得「挺像样」。
